title: Cat Cohen: Broad Strokes at the Lucille Lortel Theatre #catcohen #bro...
transcript: Cat Cohen having a stroke at age 30 is a “careful what you wish for” story. As a lifelong hypochondriac and a Leo, she's always yearned to be special — this wasn't exactly what she had in mind. Over 60 tight and zippy minutes, she recounts this experience through comedy, story, and song. There are so many autobiographical solo shows about traumatic personal experiences that carry a level of gravitas in their delivery. Refreshingly, this show doesn't do that. Though carefully crafted, it feels casual and inviting rather than self-aggrandizing. It also doesn't try to shoehorn in some corny message — comedy is the assignment here, and comedy is what we get. The material is a perfect balance between the main narrative and all these little side stories, and Cohen's cheeky and familiar stage persona is the perfect conduit for bringing sharpness and levity to such tumultuous tales. This delightfully short and sweet show is running at the Lortel through September 25th. With that, another program for my collection.
